case.title: Burst Budget
case.author_invariant: newest and older are the two most recent admitted ticks. A request is admitted exactly when older lies outside the half-open three-tick window (t-3,t]; accepted same-tick requests occupy separate budget slots and rejected requests never enter the history.

worked_value.note: Two canonical EventId-first tick-0 requests are admitted and the remaining one is rejected. At tick 3 both admissions have left (0,3], so one slot is available again.

story.premise: The surface bypass is safe but its three-tick thermal envelope permits at most two admitted switching requests. This is not a refillable token bucket: budget returns only when an actually admitted request leaves the moving window. Simultaneous requests consume distinct slots in EventId order.
story.submission: Submit a bounded controller for the exact half-open window (t-3,t], capacity two, preserving each admitted request payload and never charging rejected work.
story.diagnostics: The exhaustive oracle covers 792 bounded streams and isolates fixed-bucket resets, inclusive-boundary errors, same-tick collapse, and ghost debits from rejected requests.
hints: Remember admitted times, not arrival times.
At tick t+3, an admission from tick t has expired.
A rejected request must not shift either remembered timestamp.
